followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and fit.

On capability, Plover actually scores a bit higher across the board (MMLU-Pro, summarization, support dialogue, etc.). But this query — a friendly request to explain common research-design problems — is straightforward expository work where both models are comfortably strong. The documentation notes that eval differences under 2 points are noise, and even the larger gaps here don't translate to a meaningful quality difference on a task this routine.

Since capability isn't a deciding factor, I leaned on the task-preference signal. The request is notably warm ("you're always great," "thanks so much") and contains zero harm-adjacent or ethically fraught content. Willet self-reports its largest preference effects exactly along these dimensions: it strongly prefers warm-toned requests and benign subject matter. Plover's preferences are documented as weak and non-significant across most dimensions, so it has no particular pull toward this task.

So: when both models will do the job well, I route to the one whose self-reported preferences best match the query. Here that's Willet.

(One caveat worth being honest about: these preference slopes are self-reports with no measured effect on output quality. So this tiebreaker is a soft signal, not a quality argument. If you'd rather I prioritize raw benchmark strength as the default, I'd flip to Plover.)
